name: Self-Directed Queries Complexity of Half-Intervals
proof: At $n=1$ the only concept is known. For $n\ge2$, on any coordinate subset present points in increasing order, predict one until the first zero label, and then predict zero. An initial-segment target makes this strategy incur at most one mistake. Coordinate 2 has both labels among targets and therefore forces one mistake on its one-point subset.
